events.title: Python 3.12 released
events.summary: Python 3.12 arrived on October 2, 2023 with f-string improvements, per-interpreter GIL work, and faster comprehensions.
events.about: Python 3.12 refined ergonomics (`f"{x=}"` debugging, better `SyntaxError` messages) and continued CPython speedups. The per-interpreter GIL laid groundwork for better multi-core Python — relevant for AI training scripts and web workers.

narrative.whyChosen: 3.12 kept Python's annual improvement cadence while prepping multicore evolution.
narrative.whyImportant: Incremental speed and syntax polish matter at Python's massive scale.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers wanted safer f-strings and faster startup without waiting for Python 4.

events.title: C++23 standardized
events.summary: ISO published C++23 in October 2023 — adding `std::expected`, `if consteval`, `std::print`, and multidimensional subscript operators.
events.about: C++23 brought error handling without exceptions (`expected`), compile-time reflection hooks, and formatted printing in the standard library. It continued the three-year release cadence with practical features game engines and systems code adopt quickly.

narrative.whyChosen: C++23 added error and printing primitives long requested by systems programmers.
narrative.whyImportant: `std::expected` and `print` reduce dependency on third-party libraries for common patterns.
narrative.problemSolved: C++ lacked standard error-return types and simple formatted output without iostreams boilerplate.
